column2: Dice carrots and cucumbers into inch cubes
Mix carrots, cucumbers, cilantro,  and mix well.
Add lime juice, salt, black pepper, jeera powder just before serving
Important prep:  Rinse the chickpeas.  Add enough water and a little bit of baking soda.  Let it soak for at least 8-9 hours
Rinse the chikpeas before starting to cook.  Add fresh water to the chickpeas in a pot and salt to taste
Make a potli of tea leaves, red chillies, cinnamon stick, cardamom and bay leaves and add it to the chickpeas and start to cook the chickpeas
Cook until the chole are nice and soft.  Okay to pressure cook or open pot if the quantity is large
Finely chop the onions; puree the tomatoes and crush the ginger and garlic
In a pot heat the two oils and when hot add black cardamom, red chillies, bay leaves.  Add jeera and let it splutter
Add the ginger garlic paste and the chopped onions.  Saute until the onions are golden brown
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder and red chilly powder.  Add salt to taste and mix well
add tomato puree and cook until they turn soft and oil starts to separate
Add cooked chickpeas and let the mixture come to a boil
Add chole masala and cook on medium high flame until the gravy thickens and stir occasionally
Garnish with cilantro just before serving
Wash all the lentils 3-4 times (urad, rajma and channa dal) and soak overnight
Chop the garlic, ginger and green chillies finely
Boil/pressure cook all of the lentils with the ginger, garlic, green chillies & enough water
Use approx 3.5 times as much water as the soaked dal (or have 3 inches of water above the dal)
Simmer for 50 minutes or until lentils are well cooked
Mash the lentils lightly with the back of a ladle and add water as needed
Heat the oil in a heavy pan, add the cumin seeds and methi seeds
Add the garlic, and hing and tomato paste and stir for a minute.
Add red chilly powder and then add the tempering to the boiled dal and bring it to a boil again
Add salt, coconut milk and simmer gently for 30 minutes
Add garam masala and switch off the stove; garnish with chopped cilantro
Heat the pan and add a tbspp of oil and roughly cut onions, garlic and ginger. When onion turns translucent, add tomatoes and cashews and fry until cooked.
Set the mixture to cool completely and grind it into a smooth paste.
For gravy, heat the oil in a very low flame,  add jeera, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, jeera powder, garam masala, coriander powder and mix well in the oil until aromatic
Add the ground paste and cook well until oil seprates from the gravy
Add water, peas and salt to desirable consistency and let the gravy boil well.
In a seperate pan, heat oil/ghee and fry the paneer for 1-2 mins until the paneer turn slightly brown and keep it aside
When the gravy is fully cooked, seperate some for vegans
In the remaining gravy, add the paneer, crushed kasuri methi and cilantro and cook for 1-2 mins.
Remove some gravy before adding paneer
Add extra firm tofu and let it cook for 2-3 mins
Garnish with cilantro and crushed kasuri methi
Mixed Green Salad with Cilantro Lime dressing
Make the salad dressing by blending all the ingredients above in the vitamix.  Adjust the consistency with water as needed
Chill the dressing for an hour or so before serving
Roughly Chop Romaine lettuce, chop Cucumber and tomato into bite sized pieces
Serve with dressing on the side
Rinse and wash the black chana well. Soak in enough water overnight. Next morning pressure cook for about 6-7 whistles on medium heat, until they are tender. They shouldn't be mushy.

Heat oil add ajwain seeds, Once they splutter, add besan (if there are too many lumps in the besan, sift and use ) and sauté another 30 secs on medium-low heat or until the besan turns brown in color.
Make a paste of 1/2 cup boiled chana by adding water and add it to the tadaka
Add in the rest of the chana and mix well.
Add red chilli, turmeric, cumin-coriander powders, jaggery and tamarind water. Mix it well and sauté for another minute.

Add 1 & 1/2 cups of water, mix it well and let it cook for 8-10 minutes until the curry thickens, stirring occasionally. Adjust the consistency as per your requirement. The curry has a tendency to thicken when it gets cold.
You can add some water and reheat it to adjust the consistency.
Wash Toor dal and soak for 1-2 hours
Pressure Cook dal with turmeric and a little salt (1:3 water ratio) and then whisk it into a paste and keep it aside.
Heat oil – add mustard seeds, cumin seeds,  cloves, cinnamon, methi seeds, dried red chillies, hing
Add curry leaves, ginger paste, green chilli paste and saute well
Then add tomatoes, turmeric powder, coriander cumin powder, red chilli powder and cook till the tomatoes turn mushy
Add jaggery and tamarind paste.  Add cooked dal to this tempering
Add 4 cups of water and adjust the dal consistency as required. Add garam masala and aachar masala.
Boil it for sometime and garnish it with chopped cilantro
Boil the potatoes.  Once cooked and cooled remove the skin.  Cut into 1 inch square pieces (not very small)
Finely chop (or run through food processor) ginger, green chillies and curry leaves
Heat up oil in a pot.  Once hot add mustard seeds and let them splutter.  Add cumin seeds, hing, turmeric.
Add ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, and about 25% of the chopped cilantro.  Add salt to taste.  Saute for a minute or so
Add the potatoes and mix properly.   Lower the flame to medium low
Saute it for 7-10 minutes until the potatoes start to get browned at the bottom of the pot
Add lemon juice and mix.  Garnish with cilantro and serve
Shred the cabbage into thin, long pieces,Add salt and let it sit to remove excess water. Squeeze out the water and set aside.
Thinly slice the carrot and bell pepper.
Heat up oil in a pan. Once hot add mustard seeds, hing, green chillies and curry leaves , then add tomatoes carrot and bell Pepper.
Cook until half done, Then add all the spices ( turmeric, coriander power, garam masala, Lemon juice and sugar)
Turn off the heat and mix the cooked mixture with the shredded cabbage.
Adjust salt and lemon juice based on taste
Garnish with chopped cilantro and Green grapes
Discard the top and bottom tip of the radishes and wash well
Peel their skins and grate them through a food processor (thicker shred)
Mix the grated radishes with salt, lime juice, and cilantro.  Serve
Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times in water and soak it with 3x water and some hing and a few drops of oil for 1-2 hours
Pressure cook it:  once the pot is at full pressure reduce the heat and let it cookfor 15 minutes
Switch off the flame and let the pressure drop naturally
Once the pressure drops, open the lid and whisk the cooked dal together until its smooth
Dice the onions, bell pepper, chayote into 2 inch cubes.  Chop the tomatoes into bite sized pieces. Slightly peel and chop drumsticks into 2 inch pieces.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for an hour.  Squeeze it with your hands and remove the pulp and set aside
Heat oil and add mustard. When it splutters, add urad dhal, methi, jeera, hing. Then add red chillies and curry leaves
Add diced onions and fry until translucent. Add the tomatoes and fry until cooked.
Add the veg with water, tumeric powder and salt. Keep it covered at medium flame
When it is half-cooked, add tamarind and half of sambar powder.
Once the veg are soft, add the dhal, remaining sambar powder and salt.
When it starts boiling, reduce heat and cover for 5 mins
Garnish with some fresh tempering and cilantro
Rinse and dry the beans. Trim the ends off and cut into 1 inch pieces
Tempering: Heat oil, add mustard seeds and when it splutters, add urad dhal, jeera, hing, dry red chillies and curry leaves
Add the beans to the pan and salt. Mix well and reduce heat to low.
Then cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 15-20 mins until beans is cooked. Add little water if necessary to cook the beans. Stir well.
Add thawed frozen coconut and mix well.
Shred the cabbage into thin long pieces, and finely chop the onion.  Thaw the coconut to room temperature.  Finely chop the cilantro
Mix together cabbage, onion, coconut, cilantro, lemon juice, salt and pepper
Heat up coconut oil in a pan.  Once hot add mustard seeds, jeera, hing and curry leaves and add the tempering to the salad
Mix it all up.  Garnish with some cilantro before serving
